style: Picture a cigar-smoke back office over a social club, New York, mid-1990s, mafioso-style East Coast hip hop. The voice is an older man, fifties, gravelly and smoke-scarred, who half-raps and half-talks, flat and in no hurry, like the crew's bookkeeper walking a new kid through the accounts; quiet threat, a grin leaking through on the jokes, lagging a hair behind the kick. The loop: one muted trumpet figure circling over a plucked upright bass, slow weighty dusty boom-bap drums with a dry crack on the two and four, tape hiss, a little record crackle, lots of empty space, roughly 84 bpm. For the final couplet the band stops and only the voice is left, dry.
exclude: trap hi-hats, 808 slides, autotune, melodic singing, sung chorus, EDM, synth pads, modern pop rap, choir, bright mix
lyrics:
[Opening: muttered, unhurried, trumpet loop alone]
Uh. Uh-huh.
Money printer manual. Page one. Take notes.

[Verse: rasp, deadpan, lazy behind the beat]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

Number six: no credit? Nah, they live on the slate,
and you're paying it back in the price on your plate.

Number seven: keep the family out the business,
Treasury and the bank in one bed, God as my witness.

Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Drums and bass stop. Bare voice, close to the mic]
And the fix, from the future? Easy.
No hand on the printer.

[End]
title: tec-r1-old-gravel-mob-accountant
